claims.claim: Complement equivalence and exact endpoint cases. Let F(n,k) count labelled graphs on [n] with vertex-cover number at most k, let N=binom(n,2), and put m=n−k. For 0≤k≤n, F(n,k)=2^N−T(n,m), where T(n,m) is the number of labelled K_m-free graphs. Consequently F(n,n−3)=2^N−T(n,3), with T(n,3) the triangle-free graph count. Also F(n,0)=1; F(n,1)=1+n(2^{n−1}−1)−binom(n,2); F(n,n−2)=2^N−1; and F(n,n−1)=F(n,n)=2^N.
claims.evidence: For every graph, C is a vertex cover iff its complement is independent, so τ(G)=n−α(G). Thus τ(G)≤k iff the complement graph contains K_{n−k}, proving the count by complementation. For k=1, nonempty admissible graphs are nonempty subgraphs of a labelled star; only single-edge graphs have two possible centers, giving the stated correction. The other endpoints follow from requiring independent sets of sizes n, 2, 1, or 0. Exhaustive enumeration through n=6 confirmed every identity.
claims.search_method: Independent bijective proof, endpoint case analysis, and exhaustive exact-integer enumeration of every labelled graph for 1≤n≤6.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic exact algorithm using polynomial space and time 2^{q+O(n)}, where q=binom(n,2)−binom(n−k,2)=kn−k(k+1)/2. Therefore the target is achieved whenever k=o(n), including k=O(n/log n).
claims.evidence: For a fixed k-set C, precisely q possible edges have an endpoint in C, so exactly 2^q graphs have C as a cover. Every graph with τ≤k has at least one k-cover; retaining it only for its lexicographically first k-cover counts it exactly once. Testing all preceding covers costs poly(n)·binom(n,k)^2·2^q≤2^{q+O(n)}, while the current graph, subset indices, and an O(n²)-bit counter use polynomial space. Since q≤nk, k=o(n) makes the exponent o(n²), and O(n/log n) is included. Exact enumeration through n=6 confirmed both the generated-pair and unique-retention counts.
claims.search_method: Canonical-cover uniqueness proof, exact edge-slot count, asymptotic exponent analysis, and exhaustive small-instance verification.

claims.claim: For every fixed k there is a polynomial-time exact algorithm. More explicitly, F(n,k) is computable in time at most poly(n)·sum_{t=0}^k binom(n,t)·2^{binom(t,2)+t}·[2(t+2)]^{2^t−1}.
claims.evidence: Fix C and let I be its independent complement. If D is another cover and X=C\D, then X is independent in G[C] and U_X⊆D∩I; conversely (C\X)∪U_X is a cover. Hence C is minimum exactly when |U_X|≥|X| for every nonempty independent X. Equality describes every alternative minimum cover, and ordinary lexicographic comparison gives C<D exactly when min X<min U_X. The capped count and below-minimum flag therefore retain precisely the first minimum cover. There are at most 2^t−1 coordinates and at most 2(t+2) values per coordinate; enumerating H and neighborhood types gives the displayed fixed-k polynomial bound. Exhaustive checking validated the characterization through n=6 and reconstructed the stated DP through n=5.
claims.search_method: Complete exchange-lemma and lexicographic proof, exhaustive counterexample search through n=6, and direct implementation of the proposed exact DP through n=5.

claims.claim: Exact first- and second-moment formulas give certified bounds for all parameters. For 1≤m≤n, let q=N−binom(m,2), S1=binom(n,m)2^q, and S2=binom(n,m)·sum_{j=max(0,2m−n)}^m binom(m,j)binom(n−m,m−j)2^{N−2binom(m,2)+binom(j,2)}. Then max{2^q, ceil(S1²/S2)}≤F(n,n−m)≤min{2^N,S1}. In particular, q≤log₂F(n,n−m)≤q+n.
claims.evidence: With X(G) the number of independent m-sets, summing over one selected set gives S1. For an ordered pair intersecting in j vertices, exactly 2·binom(m,2)−binom(j,2) distinct edges are forced absent, giving the stated S2 and the full feasible j-range. The inequalities follow from 1_{X>0}≤X, Cauchy–Schwarz, and the 2^q graphs obtained by fixing one independent m-set. Finally binom(n,m)≤2^n yields the logarithmic upper bound. Exact integer summation over every graph for n≤6 confirmed both moments and all bounds.
claims.search_method: Independent ordered-pair double count, Cauchy–Schwarz proof, and exhaustive exact-integer moment evaluation for all 1≤m≤n≤6.

claims.claim: At the triangle-free endpoint, a substantial subclass is exactly countable in polynomial time. Let B_n be the number of labelled bipartite graphs and P_n=sum_{a=0}^n binom(n,a)2^{a(n−a)}. Then B_0=1 and B_n=(P_n−sum_{a=1}^{n−1}binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a})/2. Hence F(n,n−3)≤2^N−B_n is an exact-arithmetic, polynomial-time computable bound.
claims.evidence: P_n counts a graph together with an ordered proper two-coloring. Decomposing into connected components gives the labelled convolution P_n=sum_a binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a}: orient each component according to its least-labelled vertex to obtain the two B-structures, and reverse this construction uniquely. Isolating the a=0,n terms proves the recurrence. Its O(n²) exact-integer arithmetic has polynomial bit complexity. Since every bipartite graph is triangle-free, B_n≤T(n,3), so subtraction gives the asserted upper bound. Exhaustive enumeration through n=6 confirmed P_n, the recurrence, and the bound.
claims.search_method: Direct colored-component bijection, bit-complexity analysis, and exhaustive exact enumeration of bipartite and triangle-free labelled graphs through n=6.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for an exact 2^{o(n²)} algorithm uniformly for arbitrary positive input n,k. Claim 1 achieves that exponent only when k=o(n); for example, at k=floor(n/2), q=3n²/8+O(n), so its exponent remains Θ(n²). Claim 2 covers fixed k, claims 0 and 4 leave the triangle-free endpoint without an exact target-strength algorithm, and claim 3 supplies bounds rather than exact counting. These are correct and material restricted-regime results but do not resolve the uniform target. The draft explicitly calls its resolution PARTIAL and says the full target remains unresolved, so that claimed resolution is ACCURATE and not a headline overclaim.
